title: Reservation fingerprinting and credit smoothing for dedicated pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe intermittent mis-attribution of reserved throughput consumption when tenants use a mix of reserved capacity and transient burst. That leads to incorrect invoice line items and occasional over/under-issuance of SLA credits. Root causes suspected: (1) identical reservation windows being charged multiple times across sharded meters, (2) late-arriving usage events that get reclassified, and (3) imprecise tenant fingerprinting when pools host multiple reservation tiers.

Goal: Implement a deterministic reservation fingerprint + time-windowed credit smoothing to ensure idempotent attribution and graceful SLA credit calculation for partial pool degradation and tenant-level burst activity. The feature must be backward-compatible with the ledger consumer and emit migration-safe signals for downstream billing flows.
acceptance_criteria: Reservation fingerprint created per-reservation that is stable across retries and replays
Ledger events contain fingerprint and reservation effective window for every reserved throughput debit
SLA credit calculation uses a 5-minute smoothing window to avoid oscillating credits from late events
End-to-end unit test coverage for fingerprint idempotence, replay safety, and smoothing math
Integration test validates no double-billing for a tenant that moves between shards during a billing minute
design_decision: We decided to implement a 128-bit reservation fingerprint (sha256 truncated to 128 bits) composed of (pool_id, reservation_id, start_epoch_ms, tenant_id, static_nonce). The fingerprint is computed at reservation assignment time and persisted to the reservation metadata. Downstream collectors attach the fingerprint to every debit event. SLA credit smoothing will run in the billing pipeline as a separate pass that groups events by fingerprint and applies a time-decayed aggregation to produce final minutes-of-degradation per-tenant.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Emit fingerprint metadata for new reservations only; update collectors to include fingerprint on events; validate in staging. Phase 2 (migrate): Backfill fingerprints for recent active reservations via idempotent migration job for last 72 hours; enable smoothing in billing pipeline behind feature flag. Phase 3 (global): Flip feature flag after 7 days of canary, monitor billing deltas, then roll out backfill for full history if stable.
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint generation and serializer. Integration harness that replays synthetic late-arriving events and validates final ledger balances. Chaos test that simulates shard moves and verifies no duplicate debits. End-to-end billing smoke that compares billed totals pre/post smoothing for representative tenants.
